{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that Chinese readers would obtain preview benefit from word n + 2 when the preceding word (n + 1) is of relatively low frequency, testing the generality of this effect in Chinese reading.",
  "design": "mixed, 2 (preview type: identical vs. dissimilar) x 2 (boundary location: n-1 vs. n-2)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "The preview of the target word (identical vs. dissimilar) was manipulated using the gaze-contingent boundary paradigm, with the boundary placed either at the end of character n-1 or character n-2.",
  "outcome_measure": "Gaze duration on the target word (sum of all fixations on the word prior to moving to another word).",
  "population_and_setting": "36 native Chinese-speaking undergraduate students from South China Normal University.",
  "sample_size_total": 36,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Undergraduate students participating for course credit.",
  "analysis_plan": "Linear mixed models (LMM) were used to analyze gaze duration, with participants and items as crossed random effects.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used 48 experimental sentences. The target words were two-character words. The n+1 word (the character immediately to the left of the target word) was selected to have relatively low frequency (average 277 per million) to test if preview benefit for word n+2 occurs under these conditions."
